messages:
lee: quick heads up — observed a P95 latency regression on qwen2.5 after last night's kernel-selector rollout. suspected chain: kernel switched to fused-attn-cu for long sequences -> KV invalidations + tokenization splits for CJK inputs -> batch sizes dropped.

ana: ugh. saw a spike in GPU utilization too? :eyes:

lee: yes, GPU saturation up ~18% on one pod group. throughput steady but latency tails moved from ~120ms -> ~240ms for long-context flows. noticed a rise in KV cache evictions and some unexpected head dim mismatch logs.

michael: any logs/prof output? can you paste the perf counters and the kernel trace?

lee: pasted snippets below. this is from profile sampler for a 4k prompt with mixed EN/CJK:
```
# perf summary
kernel: fused-attn-cu           time=42.3ms  calls=1
kernel: matmul-quant-16         time=19.7ms  calls=3
kernel: kv-merge                time=11.1ms  calls=2
KV-cache evictions: 12 per req (prev baseline: 1-2)
batch size mean: 8 -> 3.6
```

```
# runtime debug
2026-11-03T03:12:01Z runtime: kernel-selector switched to variant 'fused-attn-cu' for model qwen2p5
2026-11-03T03:12:01Z tokenizer: split tokens increased for lang=cjk, token_count_delta=+22%
2026-11-03T03:12:01Z kvcache: head_dim_mismatch detected for kv_head=64 vs attn_head=64 (expected 64) -> fallback copy
```

zhen: head_dim_mismatch log is odd — sounds like we hit a codepath where tokenizer creates more sub-tokens and the KV head index mapping gets offset. could be an off-by-one in the multi-lang tokenizer postprocessing.

kai: i ran a quick bisect on kernel-selector heuristic locally — switching policy from `seq_len_weighted` -> `latency_estimate` reverted to previous behavior (lower latency, lower GPU util). suspect selector mis-estimated cost for fused-attn on token-sparse batches.

ana: so two interacting issues: 1) kernel selection picks fused-attn which is more GPU-bound for these mixed batches, 2) tokenizer changes increase sub-token counts for CJK which increases KV churn and reduces batching efficiency.

michael: can we try a short mitigation: pin kernel to `matmul-quant-16` for the affected route + force `tokenize_mode: conservative_cjk` to reduce splits? if that looks good, roll a canary.

lee: +1. planning to deploy a small canary to 3 pods in eu-west-1 for traffic tagged `lang:cjk` and `route:qwen2p5-long`.

runtime-bot: deploy triggered by lee: canary/qwen2p5-gpu-sat-kv/2026-11-03 03:40 UTC — 3 pods

zhen: quick note — also seeing KV-cache eviction counters sometimes spike when `kv_cache.max_entries` uses default (4096). recommend increasing to 8192 for canary to reduce evictions while we test.

kai: i added a patch to kernel-selector to include a simple correction factor: if tokenizer.cjk_ratio > 0.2 then prefer latency_estimate. PR: <link> (will attach perf runs shortly).

ana: sounds good. after canary, please capture two profiles: (A) full timeline with kernel timings and kv eviction events, (B) tokenizer token_counts per lang bucket. we need numbers to decide if we change default selector.

lee: canary deployed. will grab profiles after 30m. tagging @oncall in case rollout needs rollback.

michael: thanks. if this repros we should also add a regression test to the perf harness: mixed-lang 4k prompt with 30% CJK so we detect this in CI.

lee: agreed. collecting profiles now. will update thread with the 03:40 -> 04:10 trace.
